Grammarly review 2026 explores whether the popular writing assistant still delivers value in a market crowded with AI‑powered editors. Over the past year Grammarly has rolled out new AI models, expanded language support, and tightened integration with browsers and mobile apps. If you’re wondering if the subscription is justified for your writing needs, this guide breaks down the latest features, pricing, and real‑world performance to help you decide.

## Overview
Grammarly began as a simple grammar checker and has evolved into a full‑spectrum writing coach. The 2026 version emphasizes contextual awareness, offering suggestions that go beyond spelling to improve clarity, engagement, and delivery. It works across desktop, web, and mobile platforms, providing real‑time feedback wherever you type.

## Key Features
### Grammar Check
The core engine now uses a transformer‑based model trained on billions of sentences. It catches subtle errors like misplaced modifiers, subject‑verb agreement in complex clauses, and incorrect verb tenses that older versions missed.

### Tone Detector
Grammarly’s tone analyzer evaluates your text for formality, confidence, friendliness, and empathy. In 2026 it adds a “brand voice” matcher, letting you align your writing with predefined style guides or custom tone profiles.

### Plagiarism Checker
Integrated with academic databases and web crawlers, the plagiarism tool scans for duplicated content and provides a similarity percentage. It highlights matched sources and offers citation suggestions in APA, MLA, or Chicago formats.

### Clarity & Engagement Scores
Beyond correctness, Grammarly assigns readability scores based on sentence length, word choice, and jargon level. The engagement metric flags dull phrases and proposes more vivid alternatives to keep readers interested.

### Custom Dictionary & Snippets
Users can add industry‑specific terms to a personal dictionary and create reusable snippets for frequent phrases, speeding up workflow for professionals who write repetitive content.

## Pricing Plans
Grammarly offers three tiers in 2026:

- **Free**: Basic grammar, spelling, and punctuation checks; limited tone suggestions.
- **Premium** ($12/month billed annually): Full grammar, style, tone, plagiarism detection, and vocabulary enhancement.
- **Business** ($15 per user/month): All Premium features plus team admin dashboard, style guide enforcement, and priority support.

Discounts appear for students and educators, often reducing Premium to $8/month with a verified .edu email.

## Pros and Cons
### Pros
- Accurate, context‑aware corrections that improve over time.
- Seamless integration with Chrome, Firefox, Edge, Safari, Microsoft Office, and mobile keyboards.
- Helpful tone and clarity metrics that aid non‑native speakers.
- Robust plagiarism scanner useful for academic and professional work.

### Cons
- Premium cost may feel steep for casual users.
- Occasionally over‑aggressive suggestions that alter intended voice.
- Offline functionality limited; requires internet for full AI features.
- Plagiarism checks can be slower on large documents.

## Who Should Use It
### Students
Ideal for essays, research papers, and dissertations where grammar and originality matter. The plagiarism detector helps avoid unintentional duplication.

### Professionals
Writers, marketers, and corporate employees benefit from tone adjustments and brand‑voice alignment, ensuring consistent communication across teams.

### Non‑Native Speakers
Real‑time feedback on idiomatic usage and sentence structure accelerates language learning and boosts confidence in written English.

## FAQ
**Q: Does Grammarly work offline?**  
A: Basic spelling checks work offline, but advanced grammar, tone, and plagiarism features need an internet connection.

**Q: Is the plagiarism checker reliable for academic work?**  
A: Yes, it compares against a large database of scholarly articles and web content, though you should still verify citations manually.

**Q: Can I cancel my subscription anytime?**  
A: Yes, you can downgrade to the free plan or cancel at any point; access to premium features continues until the end of the billing period.
